title: Itanium C++ ABI
description: The cross-vendor C++ mangling: _Z prefixes, length-prefixed names. Example: `_Z3fooi` resolves to `foo(int)`.
provenance: Public record compiled from openly published documentation, project sources, and standard references.

title: MSVC mangling
description: Microsoft’s ?-prefixed scheme encoding classes, calling conventions, and types. Example: `?foo@@YAXH@Z` resolves to `void foo(int)`.
provenance: Public record compiled from openly published documentation, project sources, and standard references.

title: Rust v0 mangling
description: Rust’s _R scheme with base62 hashes and UTF-8 identifiers. Example: `_RNvC...` resolves to `crate::module::fn`.
provenance: Public record compiled from openly published documentation, project sources, and standard references.

title: Rust legacy mangling
description: The older _ZN scheme shared with C++-style paths plus a hash. Example: `_ZN3foo3barE` resolves to `foo::bar (+hash)`.
provenance: Public record compiled from openly published documentation, project sources, and standard references.

title: Swift mangling
description: Swift’s $s-prefixed scheme encoding generics, modules, and kinds. Example: `$s3foo3barV` resolves to `foo.bar struct`.
provenance: Public record compiled from openly published documentation, project sources, and standard references.

title: D (DMD) mangling
description: D’s _D-prefixed scheme with type encodings. Example: `_D3foo3barFZv` resolves to `foo.bar()`.
provenance: Public record compiled from openly published documentation, project sources, and standard references.

title: Go symbol names
description: Go uses dotted package paths, not classic mangling. Example: `main.main` resolves to `package main func main`.
provenance: Public record compiled from openly published documentation, project sources, and standard references.

title: JNI names
description: Java_ + package + class + method with underscores escaped. Example: `Java_com_foo_Bar_baz` resolves to `com.foo.Bar.baz()`.
provenance: Public record compiled from openly published documentation, project sources, and standard references.

title: gfortran underscores
description: Fortran symbols get trailing underscores, doubled on conflicts. Example: `foo_` resolves to `subroutine foo`.
provenance: Public record compiled from openly published documentation, project sources, and standard references.

title: c++filt
description: GNU binutils demangler for Itanium symbols. Example: `c++filt _Z3fooi` resolves to `foo(int)`.
provenance: Public record compiled from openly published documentation, project sources, and standard references.

title: llvm-cxxfilt
description: LLVM’s demangler handling Itanium and Rust. Example: `llvm-cxxfilt _R...` resolves to `rust symbol`.
provenance: Public record compiled from openly published documentation, project sources, and standard references.

title: undname
description: MSVC’s undname.exe decoding ?-style symbols. Example: `undname ?foo@@YAXH@Z` resolves to `void foo(int)`.
provenance: Public record compiled from openly published documentation, project sources, and standard references.

title: rustfilt
description: Demangles Rust symbols in piped output. Example: `nm a.out | rustfilt` resolves to `readable Rust paths`.
provenance: Public record compiled from openly published documentation, project sources, and standard references.

title: swift-demangle
description: Apple’s demangler for Swift symbols. Example: `swift-demangle $s...` resolves to `Swift declaration`.
provenance: Public record compiled from openly published documentation, project sources, and standard references.

title: nm --demangle
description: nm’s built-in demangling for quick symbol table reads. Example: `nm -C libfoo.a` resolves to `demangled table`.
provenance: Public record compiled from openly published documentation, project sources, and standard references.
